title: From Clinical Question to Testable Hypothesis: Using AI Co-Scientist to Identify Repurposable Drugs for Alpha-Gal Syndrome
abstract: Alpha-gal syndrome (AGS) is a tick induced, IgE-mediated allergy to the mammalian carbohydrate galactose-alpha 1,3-galactose (alpha-gal), with rising incidence and no disease modifying therapy. We describe and critically appraise a physician in the loop workflow in which a practicing clinician used Google's AI co-scientist, a multi-agent system built on the Gemini model, accessed through the experimental Hypothesis Generation tool to generate and rank drug repurposing hypotheses for AGS. Through a structured natural-language interview, the clinician defined the therapeutic goal (durable, drug-free oral tolerance permitting mammalian-meat reintroduction) and five appraisal constraints (oral route; 3–6 month course; cost <$100/month; adults 18–65, manageable side effects). The system framed the problem into three solution landscapes and returned eleven candidate directions, all built from inexpensive, oral, FDA approved medications, converging on five mechanistic themes centered on the AMPK unfolded protein response (UPR) axis. The top ranked candidate was a metformin guided, phased oral immunotherapy (OIT) protocol, followed by different combinations of metformin, zileuton, ezetimibe, ursodiol, pioglitazone and oral cromolyn. Notably, the system's review agent surfaced specific safety flaws in its own lead proposal. The workflow compressed weeks of cross disciplinary synthesis into a structured, self critiqued hypothesis set, but its outputs are hypotheses, not evidence: mechanistic assumptions are unvalidated and cited literature requires independent verification. Generative AI co-scientists can serve as a rapid, low cost ideation partner that brings a neglected disease within reach of a single clinician investigator, provided every candidate is treated as a starting point for rigorous validation.
